title.en: Volume 35: Xiong Tanlang; Zhou Di; Liu Yi; Chen Baoying
title.raw: 卷三十五 列傳第二十九: 熊曇朗 周迪 留異 陳寶應 Volume 35: Xiong Tanlang; Zhou Di; Liu Yi; Chen Baoying

sentences.zh: 陳書卷三十五

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 35
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 35

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十九

translations.literal: Biographies 29
translations.idiomatic: Biography 29

sentences.zh: 熊曇朗 周迪 留異 陳寶應

translations.literal: Xiong Tanlang; Zhou Di; Liu Yi; Chen Baoying
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tanlang; Zhou Di; Liu Yi; Chen Baoying

sentences.zh: 熊曇朗，豫章南昌人也，世為郡著姓。

translations.literal: Xiong Tanlang was a native of Nanchang in Yuzhang; for generations his family was a leading clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tanlang came from Nanchang in Yuzhang; for generations his house had been a leading clan of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 曇朗跅弛不羈，有膂力，容貌甚偉。

translations.literal: Tanlang was dissolute and unrestrained, possessed great physical strength, and had a very imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Tanlang was wild and ungoverned, powerfully built, and striking in looks.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，稍聚少年，據豐城縣為柵，桀黠劫盜多附之。

translations.literal: When the Hou Jing rebellion broke out, he gradually gathered young men, seized Fengcheng county as a palisade, and many fierce brigands and robbers joined him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hou Jing uprising he slowly gathered youths, took Fengcheng county for a stockade, and fierce raiders flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝以為巴山太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed him administrator of Bashan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang made him administrator of Bashan.

sentences.zh: 荊州陷，曇朗兵力稍彊，劫掠鄰縣，縛賣居民，山谷之中，最為巨患。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou fell, Tanlang's military strength grew somewhat; he plundered neighboring counties, bound residents and sold them; among the mountain valleys he was the greatest scourge.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingzhou fell his forces grew; he raided neighboring counties, bound commoners and sold them, and was the worst plague in the hills.

sentences.zh: 及侯瑱鎮豫章，曇朗外示服從，陰欲圖瑱。

translations.literal: When Hou Zhen garrisoned Yuzhang, Tanlang outwardly showed submission while secretly plotting against Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Zhen held Yuzhang, Tanlang feigned obedience while plotting against him in secret.

sentences.zh: 侯方兒之反瑱也，曇朗為之謀主，瑱敗，曇朗獲瑱馬仗子女甚多。

translations.literal: When Hou Fang'er rebelled against Zhen, Tanlang was the chief plotter; when Zhen was defeated, Tanlang obtained a great many of Zhen's horses, weapons, women, and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Fang'er turned on Zhen, Tanlang masterminded it; after Zhen's defeat Tanlang took a great haul of horses, arms, women, and children.

sentences.zh: 及蕭勃踰嶺，歐陽頠為前軍，曇朗紿頠共往巴山襲黃法𣰋，又報法𣰋期共破頠，約曰「事捷與我馬仗」。

translations.literal: When Xiao Bo crossed the mountains, Ouyang Yi served as vanguard; Tanlang deceived Yi into joining him on an expedition to Bashan to strike Huang Fading, while also notifying Fading of a joint appointment to break Yi, agreeing, "When the affair succeeds, give me horses and arms."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Bo crossed the range, Ouyang Yi led the van; Tanlang tricked Yi into a joint strike on Huang Fading in Bashan while telling Fading they would crush Yi together, with the bargain, "If we win, the horses and gear are mine."

sentences.zh: 及出軍，與頠掎角而進，又紿頠曰「余孝頃欲相掩襲，須分留奇兵，甲仗既少，恐不能濟」。

translations.literal: When the army marched out, it advanced pincer-wise with Yi; Tanlang again deceived Yi, saying, "Yu Xiaoding intends to ambush you—we must leave a striking force; with so few arms and armor, I fear we cannot succeed."
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he moved in concert with Yi, then lied again: "Yu Xiaoding means to ambush you—we must keep a hidden reserve; with so little armor I fear we cannot manage."

sentences.zh: 頠乃送甲三百領助之。

translations.literal: Yi then sent three hundred suits of armor to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent three hundred suits of armor to help.

sentences.zh: 及至城下，將戰，曇朗偽北，法𣰋乘之，頠失援，狼狽退衄，曇朗取其馬仗而歸。

translations.literal: When they reached the city and were about to fight, Tanlang feigned retreat; Fading pressed the pursuit; Yi lost support and withdrew in disarray; Tanlang took his horses and arms and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the walls, about to engage, Tanlang pretended flight; Fading pressed in; Yi lost his support and broke in disorder; Tanlang seized the horses and arms and went home.

sentences.zh: 時巴山陳定亦擁兵立寨，曇朗偽以女妻定子。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Ding of Bashan also held troops and built a stockade; Tanlang falsely offered his daughter to Ding's son in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ding of Bashan also held men in a fort; Tanlang falsely offered his daughter to Ding's son.

sentences.zh: 又謂定曰「周迪、余孝頃並不願此婚，必須以彊兵來迎」。

translations.literal: He also said to Ding, "Zhou Di and Yu Xiaoding both do not wish this marriage—you must send a strong force to welcome the bride."
translations.idiomatic: He told Ding, "Zhou Di and Yu Xiaoding both oppose this match—you must send a strong escort to fetch the bride."

sentences.zh: 定乃遣精甲三百并土豪二十人往迎，既至，曇朗執之，收其馬仗，並論價責贖。

translations.literal: Ding then dispatched three hundred picked troops together with twenty local strongmen to welcome her; when they arrived, Tanlang seized them, collected their horses and arms, and set a price for ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Ding sent three hundred elite troops and twenty local magnates to escort her; when they came Tanlang seized them, took horse and gear, and set a ransom.

sentences.zh: 紹泰二年，曇朗以南川豪帥，隨例除游騎將軍。

translations.literal: In Shaotai year 2, as a southern-river magnate Tanlang was by precedent made roaming-cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 2 (550), as a southern-river strongman he was made roaming-cavalry general by precedent.

sentences.zh: 尋為持節、飆猛將軍、桂州刺史資，領豐城令，歷宜新、豫章二郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was made credential-bearing, fierce-whirlwind general with acting staff as inspector of Gui prefecture, concurrently magistrate of Fengcheng, and served in succession as administrators of Yixin and Yuzhang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received the credential staff, was made fierce-whirlwind general with acting authority as inspector of Gui, held Fengcheng as magistrate, and in turn governed Yixin and Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 王琳遣李孝欽等隨余孝頃於臨川攻周迪，曇朗率所領赴援。

translations.literal: Wang Lin sent Li Xiaoqin and others with Yu Xiaoding to attack Zhou Di at Linchuan; Tanlang led his forces to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin sent Li Xiaoqin and others with Yu Xiaoding to strike Zhou Di at Linchuan; Tanlang marched to their aid.

sentences.zh: 其年，以功除持節、通直散騎常侍、寧遠將軍，封永化縣侯，邑一千戶，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: That year, for merit he was made credential-bearing, regular attendant of the fast track, pacifying-the-distance general, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yonghua with a fief of one thousand households, and granted one set of pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: That year, for merit, he was made credential-bearing fast-track regular attendant and pacifying-the-distance general, enfeoffed as Marquis of Yonghua with a thousand-household fief, and given pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 又以抗禦王琳之功，授平西將軍、開府儀同三司，餘並如故。

translations.literal: For merit in resisting Wang Lin he was further made pacifying-the-west general and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: For resisting Wang Lin he was further made pacifying-the-west general and opener equal to the three dukes; other posts stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 及周文育攻余孝勱於豫章，曇朗出軍會之，文育失利，曇朗乃害文育，以應王琳，事見文育傳。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wenyu attacked Yu Xiaomou at Yuzhang, Tanlang marched out to join him; Wenyu was defeated and Tanlang then killed Wenyu to join Wang Lin—the affair is told in Wenyu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Wenyu attacked Yu Xiaomou at Yuzhang, Tanlang came out to join him; Wenyu lost, and Tanlang killed Wenyu to answer Wang Lin—as told in Wenyu's biography.

sentences.zh: 於是盡執文育所部諸將，據新淦縣，帶江為城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized all of Wenyu's subordinate generals, held Xingan county, and walled the river bank as his city.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized all Wenyu's generals, held Xingan county, and walled the river line for a city.

sentences.zh: 王琳東下，世祖征南川兵，江州刺史周迪、高州刺史黃法𣰋欲沿流應赴，曇朗乃據城列艦斷遏，迪等與法𣰋因帥南中兵築城圍之，絕其與琳信使。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin marched east, Emperor Wen summoned southern-river troops; Zhou Di, inspector of Jiang, and Huang Fading, inspector of Gao, wished to follow the stream to answer the call; Tanlang then held the city and arrayed ships to block them; Di and the others with Fading therefore led southern troops to build walls and besiege him, cutting off his messengers with Lin.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin went east, Emperor Wen called up the southern rivers; Zhou Di of Jiang and Huang Fading of Gao meant to sail downstream to answer; Tanlang held the city and lined ships to block them; Di and Fading then led southern troops to wall and besiege him, severing his couriers to Lin.

sentences.zh: 及王琳敗走，曇朗黨援離心，迪攻陷其城，虜其男女萬餘口。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was defeated and fled, Tanlang's party and allies lost heart; Di stormed the city, capturing men and women numbering more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin was broken and fled, Tanlang's allies lost heart; Di stormed the city and took more than ten thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 曇朗走入村中，村民斬之，傳首京師，懸于朱雀觀。

translations.literal: Tanlang fled into a village; villagers beheaded him; his head was sent to the capital and hung at the Vermilion Bird Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: Tanlang fled into a hamlet; villagers cut off his head; it was sent to the capital and hung at the Vermilion Bird Observatory.

sentences.zh: [1]於是盡收其宗族，無少長皆棄市。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 1. Thereupon his entire clan was seized; none, young or old, escaped public execution.
translations.idiomatic: [1] His whole clan was then seized; young and old alike were executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 周迪，臨川南城人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Di was a native of Nancheng in Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Di came from Nancheng in Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 少居山谷，有膂力，能挽彊弩，以弋獵為事。

translations.literal: In youth he lived in the mountain valleys, possessed great strength, could draw powerful crossbows, and made his living by hunting with bow.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he lived in the hills, was powerfully built, could draw heavy crossbows, and lived by the hunt.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，迪宗人周續起兵於臨川，梁始興王蕭毅以郡讓續，迪召募鄉人從之，每戰必勇冠眾軍。

translations.literal: When the Hou Jing rebellion broke out, Di's clansman Zhou Xu raised troops in Linchuan; the Prince of Shixing of Liang, Xiao Yi, yielded the commandery to Xu; Di recruited fellow townsmen to follow him, and in every battle his courage topped all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hou Jing turmoil Di's kinsman Zhou Xu raised men in Linchuan; Liang's Prince of Shixing, Xiao Yi, yielded the commandery to Xu; Di gathered neighbors to follow, and in every fight his courage led the host.

sentences.zh: 續所部渠帥，皆郡中豪族，稍驕橫，續頗禁之，渠帥等並怨望，乃相率殺續，推迪為主，迪乃據有臨川之地，築城于工塘。

translations.literal: The commanders under Xu were all leading families of the commandery and gradually grew arrogant; Xu restrained them somewhat, and the commanders all resented it; they therefore joined to kill Xu and made Di their leader; Di then held the territory of Linchuan and built a city at Gongtang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's subordinate chiefs were all commandery magnates and grew proud; Xu checked them, and they turned resentful, killed Xu together, and set up Di; Di then held Linchuan and walled Gongtang.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝授迪持節、通直散騎常侍、壯武將軍、高州刺史，封臨汝縣侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Di credential-bearing, regular attendant of the fast track, stalwart martial general, and inspector of Gao prefecture, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Linru with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang made Di credential-bearing fast-track regular attendant and stalwart-martial general, inspector of Gao, and Marquis of Linru with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 紹泰二年，除臨川內史。

translations.literal: In Shaotai year 2 he was made interior administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 2 (550) he was made interior administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 尋授使持節、散騎常侍、信威將軍、衡州刺史，領臨川內史。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted envoy's credential staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, trustworthy-prestige general, and inspector of Heng prefecture, while still holding the interior administration of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received envoy credentials, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, trustworthy-prestige general, and the inspectorship of Heng while still governing Linchuan within.

sentences.zh: 周文育之討蕭勃也，迪按甲保境，以觀成敗。

translations.literal: When Zhou Wenyu campaigned against Xiao Bo, Di held his troops and guarded his borders, watching how the struggle would end.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Wenyu attacked Xiao Bo, Di kept his men in camp and guarded his borders, watching the outcome.

sentences.zh: 文育使長史陸山才說迪，迪乃大出糧餉，以資文育。

translations.literal: Wenyu sent his chief clerk Lu Shan'cai to persuade Di; Di then brought out grain and supplies in great quantity to supply Wenyu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu sent chief clerk Lu Shan'cai to win Di over; Di then poured out grain and stores to feed Wenyu's army.

sentences.zh: 勃平，以功加振遠將軍，遷江州刺史。

translations.literal: When Bo was pacified, for merit he was promoted to quelling-the-distance general and transferred to inspector of Jiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo was pacified, for merit he was raised to quelling-the-distance general and made inspector of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，王琳東下，迪欲自據南川，乃總召所部八郡守宰結盟，聲言入赴，朝廷恐其為變，因厚慰撫之。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication and Wang Lin marched east, Di wished to hold the southern rivers for himself; he therefore summoned the administrators of eight commanderies under him to swear alliance, claiming he would enter to answer the call; the court feared he would turn rebel and therefore treated him with rich consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne and Wang Lin went east, Di meant to keep the southern rivers; he called the eight commandery heads to swear alliance, saying he would march to answer the summons; the court feared revolt and soothed him generously.

sentences.zh: 琳至湓城，新吳洞主余孝頃舉兵應琳。

translations.literal: When Lin reached Poyang, Yu Xiaoding, lord of the Xinwu cave settlement, raised troops to answer Lin.
translations.idiomatic: At Poyang, Xinwu cave lord Yu Xiaoding rose for Lin.

sentences.zh: 琳以為南川諸郡可傳檄而定，乃遣其將李孝欽、樊猛等南征糧餉。

translations.literal: Lin thought the southern-river commanderies could be settled by proclamation alone and therefore sent his generals Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and others south to gather grain.
translations.idiomatic: Lin judged the southern commanderies would fall to a proclamation and sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and others south for grain.

sentences.zh: 猛等與余孝頃相合，眾且二萬，來趨工塘，連八城以逼迪。

translations.literal: Meng and the others joined Yu Xiaoding; their forces were nearly twenty thousand; they came pressing on Gongtang, linking eight forts to corner Di.
translations.idiomatic: Meng joined Yu Xiaoding; together they neared twenty thousand men and pressed Gongtang, chaining eight forts against Di.

sentences.zh: 迪使周敷率眾頓臨川故郡，截斷江口，因出與戰，大敗之，屠其八城，生擒李孝欽、樊猛、余孝頃送于京師，收其軍實，器械山積，并虜其人馬，迪並自納之。

translations.literal: Di sent Zhou Fu to lead troops and encamp at the old seat of Linchuan commandery, cutting off the river mouth; he then came out to fight, routed them utterly, slaughtered the eight forts, and sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoding alive to the capital; he collected their military stores—arms piled like hills—and also captured their men and horses, which Di kept for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Di sent Zhou Fu to hold the old Linchuan seat and choke the river mouth, then sallied and crushed them, razed the eight forts, and sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoding alive to court; arms and stores heaped like hills—and men and horses Di kept.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，以功加平南將軍、開府儀同三司，增邑一千五百戶，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In Yongding year 2, for merit he was promoted to pacifying-the-south general and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes; his fief was increased by one thousand five hundred households, and he was granted one set of pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2 (558), for merit he was made pacifying-the-south general and opener equal to the three dukes, with fifteen hundred more households and pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 世祖嗣位，進號安南將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Di's title was advanced to pacifying-the-south general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Di was advanced to pacifying-the-south general.

sentences.zh: [2]熊曇朗之反也，迪與周敷、黃法𣰋等率兵共圍曇朗，屠之，盡有其眾。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 2. When Xiong Tanlang rebelled, Di with Zhou Fu, Huang Fading, and others led troops together to besiege Tanlang, slaughtered him, and wholly took over his following.
translations.idiomatic: [2] When Xiong Tanlang rebelled, Di with Zhou Fu and Huang Fading jointly besieged him, destroyed him, and absorbed all his men.

sentences.zh: 王琳敗後，世祖徵迪出鎮湓城，又徵其子入朝，迪趑趄顧望，並不至。

translations.literal: After Wang Lin was defeated, Emperor Wen summoned Di to go out and garrison Poyang and also summoned his son to court; Di hesitated and looked back and forth, and neither came.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Lin's defeat, Emperor Wen called Di to garrison Poyang and his son to court; Di wavered and would not come—neither of them.

sentences.zh: 豫章太守周敷本屬於迪，至是與黃法𣰋率其所部詣闕，世祖錄其破熊曇朗之功，並加官賞，迪聞之，甚不平，乃陰與留異相結。

translations.literal: The administrator of Yuzhang, Zhou Fu, had originally been subordinate to Di; at this time he with Huang Fading led their commands to the capital; Emperor Wen recorded their merit in breaking Xiong Tanlang and both added rank and reward; when Di heard it he was very resentful and therefore secretly joined with Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhang administrator Zhou Fu had once served Di; now he and Huang Fading brought their troops to court; Emperor Wen credited their part in breaking Tanlang and heaped honors on them; Di, hearing it, burned with resentment and secretly allied with Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 及王師討異，迪疑懼不自安，乃使其弟方興率兵襲周敷，敷與戰，破之。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Yi, Di in suspicion and fear could not be at ease; he therefore sent his younger brother Fangxing to lead troops and strike Zhou Fu; Fu fought and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved on Liu Yi, Di, uneasy with fear, sent his brother Fangxing against Zhou Fu; Fu met him and broke him.

sentences.zh: 又別使兵襲華皎於湓城，事覺，盡為皎所擒。

translations.literal: He also separately sent troops to strike Hua Jiao at Poyang; the affair was discovered and they were all seized by Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent another force against Hua Jiao at Poyang; the plot came out and Jiao seized them all.

sentences.zh: 〔天嘉〕三年春，[3]世祖乃下詔赦南川士民為迪所詿誤者，使江州刺史吳明徹都督眾軍，與高州刺史黃法𣰋、豫章太守周敷討迪。

translations.literal: Collation variant: (Tianjia). In the third year, spring, Editorial footnote marker 3. Emperor Wen then issued an edict pardoning the southern-river gentry and commoners misled by Di, and ordered Wu Mingche, inspector of Jiang, to command all armies together with Huang Fading, inspector of Gao, and Zhou Fu, administrator of Yuzhang, to campaign against Di.
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Tianjia). In spring of the third year, [3] Emperor Wen pardoned southern-river people led astray by Di and ordered Jiang inspector Wu Mingche to command all forces with Gao inspector Huang Fading and Yuzhang administrator Zhou Fu against Di.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書下符曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon the Masters of Writing issued a warrant, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing then issued a warrant, saying:

sentences.zh: 告臨川郡士庶：昔西京為盛，信、越背誕；

translations.literal: To the gentry and commoners of Linchuan commandery: In ancient times the Western Capital flourished, yet Xin and Yue turned disloyal;
translations.idiomatic: To the people of Linchuan: In old days the Western Capital stood in glory, yet Xin and Yue turned traitor;

sentences.zh: 東都中興，萌、寵違戾。

translations.literal: when the Eastern Capital revived, Yin and Chong defied allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: when the Eastern Capital rose again, Yin and Chong broke faith.

sentences.zh: 是以鷹鸇競逐，效醢極誅，自古有之，其來尚矣。

translations.literal: Therefore hawk and eagle contend in pursuit, and punishments of mincing extend to execution—since antiquity this has existed, and its origins are very old.
translations.idiomatic: So hawk and eagle hunt one another, and the extreme penalty of mincing has been known from of old—its roots run deep.

sentences.zh: 逆賊周迪，本出輿臺，有梁喪亂，暴掠山谷。

translations.literal: The rebel Zhou Di was originally of low station; in Liang's time of ruin he ravaged the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhou Di sprang from humble ranks; in Liang's collapse he plundered the hills.

sentences.zh: 我高祖躬率百越，師次九川，濯其泥沙，假以毛羽，裁解豚佩，仍剖獸符，[4]卵翼之恩，方斯莫喻。

translations.literal: Our Founder personally led the hundred Yue, halted his army at the nine rivers, washed away their mud and sand and lent them feather and down, cut the pig tally and apportioned the beast seal—Editorial footnote marker 4.—fostering kindness such as no other equals.
translations.idiomatic: Our Founder himself led the hundred Yue, halted at the nine rivers, washed mud from them and lent them feather and down, cut the pig tally and split the beast seal—[4]—a brooding kindness none could match.

sentences.zh: 皇運肇基，頗布誠款，國步艱阻，竟微效力。

translations.literal: When the imperial fortune first took root, he broadly showed good faith, yet amid the state's hard straits he scarcely rendered service.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty's fortune began he showed good faith, yet in the state's distress he barely served.

sentences.zh: 龍節繡衣，藉王爵而御下，熊旗組甲，因地險而陵上。

translations.literal: With dragon tally and embroidered robe he borrowed royal rank to rule those below; with bear banner and linked armor he relied on rugged ground to look down on his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon tally and embroidered robe let him rule from borrowed rank; bear banner and mail let him tower from rugged ground over his betters.

sentences.zh: 日者王琳始貳，蕭勃未夷，西結三湘，南通五嶺，衡、廣戡定，既安反側，江、郢紛梗，復生攜背，擁據一郡，苟且百心，志貌常違，言跡不副。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin first turned disloyal and Xiao Bo was not yet pacified, he joined the three Xiang in the west and the five ranges in the south; when Heng and Guang were settled and the rebellious were calmed, the Jiang and Ying regions were again in turmoil and treachery rose anew—he held a single commandery, clinging to a hundred shifting hearts, his intent and bearing always at odds, his words and tracks never matching.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin first wavered and Xiao Bo still stood, he tied to the three Xiang westward and the five ranges southward; Heng and Guang were quieted and rebels steadied, yet Jiang and Ying stirred again—he clutched one commandery with a hundred fickle hearts, face and deed ever at odds, word and trail never aligned.

sentences.zh: 特以新吳未靜，地遠兵彊，互相兼并，成其形勢。

translations.literal: Only because Xinwu was not yet settled and the land was remote with strong troops did mutual swallowing make his power.
translations.idiomatic: Only while Xinwu stayed unsettled and distant ground bred strong arms did mutual swallowing build his strength.

sentences.zh: 收獲器械，俘虜士民，並曰私財，曾無獻捷。

translations.literal: He collected arms and gear and captured gentry and commoners, calling them all private property, and never once reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: Arms he gathered, people he seized, and called it all private spoil—never once reporting victory to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時遣一介，終持兩端。

translations.literal: When the court sent a single envoy, he always held to two sides.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent one envoy, he still straddled both sides.

sentences.zh: 朝廷光大含弘，引納崇遇，遂乃位等三槐，任均四嶽，富貴隆赫，超絕功臣。

translations.literal: The court in its vast forbearance drew him in with high honor; he then stood equal to the Three Hushes and shared duty with the Four Peaks—wealth and rank towering, surpassing all meritorious servants.
translations.idiomatic: The court, broad in mercy, drew him close with honor until he ranked with the Three Hushes and shared the Four Peaks' burden—wealth and title towering above every merit-holder.

sentences.zh: 加以出師逾嶺，遠相響援，按甲斷江，翻然猜拒。

translations.literal: Moreover, when armies crossed the ranges he answered from afar; he held his troops and blocked the river, then suddenly turned suspicious and defiant.
translations.idiomatic: When armies crossed the hills he answered from afar; he held his men and barred the river, then turned sudden and defiant.

sentences.zh: 故司空愍公，敦以宗盟，情同骨肉，城池連接，勢猶脣齒，彭亡之禍，坐觀難作，階此舋故，結其黨與。

translations.literal: The late Minister of Works, the Lamented Duke, treated him as kin by clan pact, close as flesh and bone; their walled cities adjoined, their strength like lips and teeth; yet at the disaster of Pengwang he sat and watched difficulty arise—on that grievance he bound his faction.
translations.idiomatic: The late lamented Minister of Works treated him as sworn kin, bone to bone; their walls touched, strength like lips and teeth—yet at Pengwang's ruin he only watched trouble grow, and on that grudge knit his faction.

sentences.zh: 于時北寇侵軼，西賊憑陵，屝屨糇糧，悉以資寇，爵號軍容，一遵偽黨。

translations.literal: At that time northern invaders pressed the borders and western rebels leaned on the land; sandals and grain he wholly supplied to the enemy; rank and military display he wholly followed the false party.
translations.idiomatic: Northern raiders then pressed the frontier and western rebels leaned on the land; sandals and grain he fed the foe; rank and martial show he copied the rebel host.

sentences.zh: 及王師凱振，大定區中，天網恢弘，棄之度外，璽書綸誥，撫慰綢繆，冠蓋縉紳，敦授重疊。

translations.literal: When the imperial army returned in triumph and greatly settled the realm, the heavenly net was broad and cast him beyond its mesh; with imperial writs and edicts the court soothed him again and again; caps and girdles of office-holders were heaped upon him in layers.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial host returned victorious and the realm was largely settled, heaven's net was wide and set him outside it—yet edict on edict soothed him, honors on honors from the girdled ranks.

sentences.zh: 至於熊曇朗勦滅，豐城克定，蓋由儀同法𣰋之元功，安西周敷之效力，司勳有典，懋賞斯舊，惡直醜正，自為仇讎，悖禮姦謀，因此滋甚。

translations.literal: As for the slaughter of Xiong Tanlang and the taking of Fengcheng, that was chiefly the founding merit of Equal-in-Honor Fading and the exertion of pacifying-the-west Zhou Fu; the Ministry of Awards has its canon and rich reward is the old rule—yet he hated the upright and loathed the true, making himself their enemy; against ritual and in secret plot he therefore grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of Xiong Tanlang and Fengcheng came chiefly from Fading's founding merit and Fu's exertion—the Ministry of Awards keeps its rule and rich reward is ancient custom—yet he hated the upright, made enemies of the true, and against ritual and in secret plot grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 徵出湓城，歷年不就，求遣侍子，累載未朝。

translations.literal: Summoned to leave Poyang, for years he would not come; asked to send a son to attend court, for years the boy did not present himself.
translations.idiomatic: Called from Poyang, he would not come for years; asked for a son at court, the boy stayed away for years.

sentences.zh: 外誘逋亡，招集不逞，中調京輦，規冀非常。

translations.literal: Outwardly he lured fugitives and gathered the ungoverned; inwardly he stirred the capital, scheming for the extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Outside he lured fugitives and gathered rowdies; inside he stirred the capital, scheming the unthinkable.

sentences.zh: 擅斂征賦，罕歸九府，擁遏二賈，害及四民。

translations.literal: He levied taxes on his own authority and rarely sent revenue to the nine treasuries; he blocked the two merchant routes and harmed the four classes of people.
translations.idiomatic: He taxed on his own and seldom sent coin to the nine treasuries; he choked the two trade roads and hurt the four orders of folk.

sentences.zh: 潛結賊異，共為表裏，同惡相求，密加應援。

translations.literal: He secretly joined the rebel Yi, inside and outside as one garment; seeking the same evil, they aided each other in secret.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly joined rebel Liu Yi, outer and inner as one coat; alike in evil, they answered each other in secret.

sentences.zh: 謂我六軍薄伐，三越未寧，屠破述城，虜縛妻息，分襲湓鎮，稱兵蠡邦，拘逼酋豪，攻圍城邑，幸國有備，應時衄殄。

translations.literal: He thought our six armies' shallow campaign and the three Yue not yet settled—when we slaughtered and broke Shucheng, bound wives and children, and separately struck the Poyang garrison, he raised arms in the Li country, coerced tribal chiefs, and besieged walled cities; fortunate that the state was prepared, he was beaten and destroyed at once.
translations.idiomatic: He judged our six hosts' light campaign and the three Yue still restless—yet when we broke Shucheng, seized wives and children, and struck Poyang apart, he raised arms in the Li lands, coerced chiefs, and besieged towns; the state was ready, and he was crushed at once.

sentences.zh: 假節、通直散騎常侍、仁武將軍、尋陽太守懷仁縣伯華皎，明威將軍、廬陵太守益陽縣子陸子隆，並破賊徒，剋全郡境。

translations.literal: Acting on credential, fast-track regular attendant, humane-martial general, and administrator of Xunyang, Marquis of Huairen, Hua Jiao, and bright-prestige general, administrator of Luling, Viscount of Yiyang, Lu Zilong, both broke the rebel bands and recovered their commandery territories whole.
translations.idiomatic: Acting-credential fast-track regular attendant, humane-martial general, Xunyang administrator, Marquis of Huairen Hua Jiao, and bright-prestige general, Luling administrator, Viscount of Yiyang Lu Zilong, both broke the rebels and restored their commanderies entire.

sentences.zh: 持節、散騎常侍、安西將軍、定州刺史、[5]領豫章太守西豐縣侯周敷，躬扞溝壘，身當矢石，率茲義勇，以寡摧眾，斬馘萬計，俘虜千群。

translations.literal: Credential-bearing, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-west general, inspector of Ding prefecture, Editorial footnote marker 5. concurrently administrator of Yuzhang, Marquis of Xifeng, Zhou Fu, himself defended the ditch and rampart and took the arrows and stones; leading these loyal and brave men, with few he crushed many—heads and ears by the tens of thousands, captives by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Credential-bearing scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-west general, Ding inspector, [5] and Yuzhang administrator, Marquis of Xifeng Zhou Fu, manned ditch and wall and stood in the arrow storm; with loyal courage and few men he broke many—tens of thousands slain, thousands taken.

sentences.zh: 迪方收餘燼，還固墉堞。

translations.literal: Di was then gathering the last embers and returning to hold the walls and towers.
translations.idiomatic: Di was gathering embers and clinging again to wall and tower.

sentences.zh: 使持節、安南將軍、開府儀同三司、高州刺史新建縣侯法𣰋，雄績早宣，忠誠夙著，未奉王命，前率義旅，既援敷等，又全子隆，裹糧擐甲，仍躡飛走，批羆之旅，驅馳越電，振武之眾，叱吒移山，以此追奔，理無遺類。

translations.literal: Envoy-credential, pacifying-the-south general, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, inspector of Gao prefecture, Marquis of Xinjian, Fading, had long shown heroic achievement and from of old stood in loyalty; before he received the royal command he had led loyal troops of his own; he both aided Fu and the others and wholly saved Zilong; wrapping grain and donning armor he still pursued the flying foe; troops that beat the bear ran faster than lightning; warriors who shook mountains shouted and moved peaks—with such pursuit none should remain.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy-credential pacifying-the-south general, opener equal to the three dukes, Gao inspector, Marquis of Xinjian Fading, had shown heroism early and loyalty long; before royal orders he led loyal troops, aided Fu, and saved Zilong whole—grain wrapped, armor on, still chasing the flying foe; bear-beating hosts outran lightning; mountain-shaking warriors shouted hills aside—by such pursuit none should escape.

sentences.zh: 雖復朽株將拔，非待尋斧，落葉就殞，無勞烈風；

translations.literal: Though a rotten stump is about to fall and needs no second axe, and fallen leaves are about to perish and need no fierce wind;
translations.idiomatic: Though a rotten stump will fall without a second axe, and fallen leaves will die without a gale wind;

sentences.zh: 但去草絕根，在於未蔓，撲火止燎，貴乎速滅，分命將帥，寔資英果。

translations.literal: yet to uproot weeds one must act before they spread, and to stamp out fire one must value quick extinction; dividing orders among generals truly relies on heroic decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: yet weeds are uprooted before they spread, and fire is quenched while the blaze is small—orders divided among generals truly need heroic fruit.

sentences.zh: 今遣鎮南儀同司馬、湘東公相劉廣德，兼平西司馬孫曉，北新蔡太守魯廣達，持節、安南將軍、吳州刺史彭澤縣侯魯悉達，甲士萬人，步出興口。

translations.literal: Now we send the pacifying-the-south equal-in-honor's marshal of the army, Xiangdong Duke's chancellor Liu Guangde, together with pacifying-the-west marshal Sun Xiao, administrator of North Xin'ai Lu Guangda, credential-bearing pacifying-the-south general, inspector of Wu prefecture, Marquis of Pengze Lu Xida, with ten thousand armored men, marching out from Xingkou.
translations.idiomatic: We now send pacifying-the-south equal-in-honor's army marshal, Xiangdong duke's chancellor Liu Guangde, with pacifying-the-west marshal Sun Xiao, North Xin'ai administrator Lu Guangda, credential-bearing pacifying-the-south general and Wu inspector Marquis of Pengze Lu Xida, and ten thousand armored men, marching from Xingkou.

sentences.zh: 又遣前吳興太守胡鑠，樹功將軍、前宣城太守錢法成，天門、義陽二郡太守樊毅，雲麾將軍、合州刺史南固縣侯焦僧度，嚴武將軍、建州刺史辰縣子張智達，持節、都督江吳二州諸軍事、安南將軍、江州刺史安吳縣侯吳明徹，樓艦馬步，直指臨川。

translations.literal: We also send the former administrator of Wu Xing, Hu Shuo, the merit-establishing general and former administrator of Xuancheng Qian Facheng, the administrators of Tianmen and Yiyang, Fan Yi, the cloud-banner general and inspector of He prefecture, Marquis of Nangu, Jiao Sengdu, the stern-martial general and inspector of Jian prefecture, Viscount of Chen, Zhang Zhida, and credential-bearing commander of Jiang and Wu regions, pacifying-the-south general, inspector of Jiang prefecture, Marquis of Anwu, Wu Mingche, with tower ships, horse, and foot, pointing straight at Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: We also send former Wu Xing administrator Hu Shuo, merit-establishing general and former Xuancheng administrator Qian Facheng, Tianmen and Yiyang administrators Fan Yi, cloud-banner general and He inspector Marquis of Nangu Jiao Sengdu, stern-martial general and Jian inspector Viscount of Chen Zhang Zhida, and credential-bearing commander of Jiang and Wu, pacifying-the-south general, Jiang inspector Marquis of Anwu Wu Mingche, with tower ships and horse and foot straight at Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 前安成內史劉士京，巴山太守蔡僧貴，南康內史劉峰，廬陵太守陸子隆，安成內史闕慎，並受儀同法𣰋節度，同會故郡。

translations.literal: The former interior administrator of Ancheng, Liu Shijing, the administrator of Bashan, Cai Senggui, the interior administrator of Nankang, Liu Feng, the administrator of Luling, Lu Zilong, and the interior administrator of Ancheng, Que Shen, all receive Fading's command and will assemble at the old commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: Former Ancheng interior administrator Liu Shijing, Bashan administrator Cai Senggui, Nankang interior administrator Liu Feng, Luling administrator Lu Zilong, and Ancheng interior administrator Que Shen all take Fading's orders and meet at the old commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 又命尋陽太守華皎，光烈將軍、巴州刺史潘純陀，平西將軍、郢州刺史欣樂縣侯章昭達，並率貔豹，逕造賊城。

translations.literal: We also order the administrator of Xunyang, Hua Jiao, the bright-blaze general and administrator of Ba prefecture, Pan Chuntuo, the pacifying-the-west general and inspector of Ying prefecture, Marquis of Xinle, Zhang Zhaoda, all to lead tiger hosts and go straight to the rebel city.
translations.idiomatic: We also order Xunyang administrator Hua Jiao, bright-blaze general and Ba administrator Pan Chuntuo, and pacifying-the-west general and Ying inspector Marquis of Xinle Zhang Zhaoda, each leading tiger troops straight to the rebel city.

sentences.zh: 使持節、散騎常侍、鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司、湘州刺史湘東郡公度，分遣偏裨，相繼上道，戈船蔽水，彀騎彌山。

translations.literal: Envoy-credential, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-south general, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, inspector of Xiang prefecture, Duke of Xiangdong commandery, Du, dispatches wing commanders in succession on the road; war boats cover the water and armored horsemen fill the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy-credential scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-south general, opener equal to the three dukes, Xiang inspector, Duke of Xiangdong Du, sends wing after wing on the road—war boats blanket the water, armored riders the hills.

sentences.zh: 又詔鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司歐陽頠，率其子弟交州刺史盛、新除太子右率邃、衡州刺史侯曉等，[6]以勁越之兵，踰嶺北邁。

translations.literal: We also command pacifying-the-south general and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes Ouyang Yi to lead his sons—the inspector of Jiao prefecture Sheng, the newly appointed right leader of the crown prince's guard Sui, the inspector of Heng prefecture Hou Xiao, and others—Editorial footnote marker 6.—with strong Yue troops to cross the ranges northward.
translations.idiomatic: We also command pacifying-the-south general and opener equal to the three dukes Ouyang Yi to lead his sons—Jiao inspector Sheng, the newly made crown-prince right leader Sui, Heng inspector Hou Xiao, and others—[6]—with hard Yue troops over the ranges north.

sentences.zh: 千里同期，百道俱集，如脫稽誅，更淹旬晦，司空、大都督安都已平賊異，凱歸非久，飲至禮畢，乘勝長驅，勦撲凶醜，如燎毛髮。

translations.literal: A thousand li on the same schedule, a hundred roads all gathering—if we delay execution even another ten days and half a month, the Minister of Works, grand commander, will already have pacified the rebel Yi and returned in triumph not long after; when the drinking ceremony is complete we shall drive the victory in a long pursuit and stamp out the vicious, like singeing hair.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li on one timetable, a hundred roads converging—if we linger on punishment another fortnight, the Minister of Works and grand commander will already have pacified Liu Yi and soon return victorious; when the drinking rite ends we drive the victory straight on and stamp the vicious out like singeing hair.

sentences.zh: 已有明詔，罪唯迪身，黎民何辜，一皆原宥。

translations.literal: There is already a clear edict: guilt rests on Di alone; what crime have the people? All are pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: A clear edict already states: guilt is Di's alone; what fault have the people? All are forgiven.

sentences.zh: 其有因機立功，賞如別格；

translations.literal: Whoever by the occasion establishes merit will be rewarded according to a separate statute;
translations.idiomatic: Whoever seizes the moment for merit will be rewarded by separate statute;

sentences.zh: 執迷不改，刑茲罔赦。

translations.literal: whoever clings to error and does not change, punishment knows no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: whoever clings to error unchanged, the law knows no mercy.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹至臨川，令眾軍作連城攻迪，相拒不能剋，世祖乃遣高宗總督討之，迪眾潰，妻子悉擒，乃脫身踰嶺之晉安，依于陳寶應。

translations.literal: When Wu Mingche reached Linchuan he ordered the armies to build linked walls to attack Di; they faced each other and could not overcome him; Emperor Wen then sent Emperor Gaozong to take overall command of the campaign; Di's host collapsed; wives and children were all seized; he alone slipped away over the ranges to Jin'an and relied on Chen Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche reached Linchuan and ordered linked siegeworks against Di; they faced each other without victory; Emperor Wen then sent Emperor Gaozong to command the campaign overall; Di's men collapsed, wife and children all taken; he alone fled over the ranges to Jin'an and clung to Chen Baoying.

sentences.zh: 寶應以兵資迪，留異又遣第二子忠臣隨之。

translations.literal: Baoying supplied Di with troops and stores; Liu Yi also sent his second son, the Loyal Subject, to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying armed Di with troops and stores; Liu Yi also sent his second son, the Loyal Subject, to follow.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，復越東興嶺，東興、南城、永成縣民，皆迪故人，復共應之。

translations.literal: The next autumn he again crossed the Dongxing range; the people of Dongxing, Nancheng, and Yongcheng counties were all Di's old associates and again answered him together.
translations.idiomatic: Next autumn he crossed Dongxing Pass again; people of Dongxing, Nancheng, and Yongcheng were all his old ties and rose for him once more.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣都督章昭達征迪，迪又散于山谷。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent the commander Zhang Zhaoda to campaign against Di; Di again scattered into the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent commander Zhang Zhaoda against Di; Di again melted into the hills.

sentences.zh: 初，侯景之亂也，百姓皆棄本業，群聚為盜，唯迪所部，獨不侵擾，並分給田疇，督其耕作，民下肆業，各有贏儲，政教嚴明，徵斂必至，餘郡乏絕者，皆仰以取給。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Hou Jing rebellion broke out, the common people all abandoned their proper occupations and gathered as bandits; only in the territory under Di's rule was there no plundering; he even divided fields among them, supervised their farming, and the people pursued their trades—each had surplus stores; his government and teaching were strict and clear, and levies always arrived; commanderies that lacked supplies all looked to him for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hou Jing turmoil commoners had abandoned their trades and banded as robbers; only under Di was there no looting—he parceled fields, oversaw farming, and folk worked their trades with surplus in every storehouse; rule was strict, levies sure, and needy commanderies lived on his grain.

sentences.zh: 迪性質朴，不事威儀，冬則短身布袍，夏則紫紗袜腹，居常徒跣，雖外列兵衛，內有女伎，挼繩破篾，傍若無人。

translations.literal: Di's nature was plain and simple; he did not attend to ceremonial display; in winter he wore a short cloth robe, in summer a purple-gauze belly-wrap; in daily life he went barefoot; though outwardly he arrayed guards and soldiers, inwardly he had female performers; twisting rope and splitting bamboo, he was as if no one were present.
translations.idiomatic: Di was plain by nature and cared nothing for display; in winter a short cloth coat, in summer a purple gauze belly-wrap; usually barefoot; though guards stood without, singers within, he twisted rope and split bamboo as if alone.

sentences.zh: 然輕財好施，凡所周贍，毫釐必鈞，訥於言語，而襟懷信實，臨川人皆德之。

translations.literal: Yet he was light with wealth and fond of giving; in all he aided, even the smallest measure was weighed with a balance; he was slow of speech yet his breast was faithful and true—the people of Linchuan all blessed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was free with wealth and loved to give; every gift he weighed to the hair; slow of tongue but faithful in heart—the people of Linchuan all honored him.

sentences.zh: 至是並共藏匿，雖加誅戮，無肯言者。

translations.literal: At this time they all hid him together; though punishments were heaped on them, none would speak.
translations.idiomatic: Now they hid him together; though execution pressed them, none would tell.

sentences.zh: 昭達仍度嶺，頓于建安，與陳寶應相抗，迪復收合出東興。

translations.literal: Zhaoda then crossed the range and encamped at Jian'an, resisting Chen Baoying; Di again gathered his forces and came out at Dongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoda crossed the pass and camped at Jian'an against Chen Baoying; Di gathered men again and came out at Dongxing.

sentences.zh: 時宣城太守錢肅鎮東興，以城降迪。

translations.literal: At the time Qian Su, administrator of Xuancheng, garrisoned Dongxing and yielded the city to Di.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng administrator Qian Su then held Dongxing and surrendered the city to Di.

sentences.zh: 吳州刺史陳詳，率師攻迪，詳兵大敗，虔化侯陳訬、陳留太守張遂並戰死，於是迪眾復振。

translations.literal: Wu prefecture inspector Chen Xiang led troops to attack Di; Xiang's army was greatly defeated; Marquis of Qianhua Chen Xu and Chenliu prefect Zhang Sui both died in battle; thereupon Di's host revived.
translations.idiomatic: Wu prefect Chen Xiang marched against Di and was routed. Marquis of Qianhua Chen Xu and Chenliu prefect Zhang Sui fell in battle, and Di's forces rallied again.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣都督程靈洗擊破之，迪又與十餘人竄于山穴中，日月轉久，相隨者亦稍苦之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent area commander Cheng Lingxi to defeat them; Di again fled into mountain caves with more than ten men; days and months passed and those who followed him gradually grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent area commander Cheng Lingxi to break them. Di fled into the hills with a dozen men. Time wore on, and even his companions began to suffer.

sentences.zh: 後遣人潛出臨川郡市魚鮭，足痛，舍於邑子，邑子告臨川太守駱牙，牙執之，令取迪自效。

translations.literal: Later he sent men out secretly to buy fish at Linchuan commandery market; his feet ached and he lodged with a village man; the villager reported to Linchuan prefect Luo Ya; Ya seized him and ordered him to bring Di in to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sent men secretly to buy fish at the Linchuan market. His feet pained him, and he stayed with a villager, who told Linchuan prefect Luo Ya. Ya seized him and ordered him to deliver Di alive.

sentences.zh: 因使腹心勇士隨入山中，誘迪出獵，伏兵於道傍，斬之，傳首京都，梟于朱雀觀三日。

translations.literal: He then sent loyal brave warriors to follow into the mountains, lure Di out hunting, and set ambush along the road; they beheaded him, sent the head to the capital, and exposed it at Vermilion Bird Observatory for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He sent trusted warriors into the hills to lure Di out hunting, ambushed him on the road, and beheaded him. The head went to the capital and hung three days at Vermilion Bird Observatory.

sentences.zh: 留異，東陽長山人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yi was a man of Changshan in Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi came from Changshan in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 世為郡著姓。

translations.literal: His family for generations were a prominent surname of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his clan ranked among the commandery's leading families.

sentences.zh: 異善自居處，言語醞藉，為鄉里雄豪。

translations.literal: Yi was skilled at deportment; his speech urbane and refined; he was a local strongman.
translations.idiomatic: Yi carried himself well and spoke with polished ease; he was a local magnate.

sentences.zh: 多聚惡少，陵侮貧賤，守宰皆患之。

translations.literal: He gathered many ruffians, bullied poor and lowly; magistrates all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered ruffians and bullied the poor; every magistrate feared him.

sentences.zh: 梁代為蟹浦戍主，歷晉安、安固二縣令。

translations.literal: In Liang times he was garrison chief at Xiepu and served as magistrate of Jin'an and Angu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he was garrison chief at Xiepu and magistrate of Jin'an and Angu in turn.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，還鄉里，召募士卒，東陽郡丞與異有隙，引兵誅之，及其妻子。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled he returned to his home district and recruited soldiers; the Dongyang commandery aide had a feud with Yi and led troops to execute him and his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled he went home and raised troops. The Dongyang commandery aide, who hated him, led soldiers to kill Yi and his family.

sentences.zh: 太守沈巡援臺，讓郡於異，異使兄子超監知郡事，率兵隨巡出都。

translations.literal: Prefect Shen Xun went to aid the capital and yielded the commandery to Yi; Yi had his nephew Chao oversee commandery affairs and led troops following Xun to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Shen Xun went to relieve the capital and yielded the commandery to Yi. Yi set his nephew Chao to run the commandery and marched with Xun to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及京城陷，異隨臨城公蕭大連，大連板為司馬，委以軍事。

translations.literal: When the capital fell Yi followed Prince of Lincheng Xiao Dalian; Dalian commissioned him marshal and entrusted him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell Yi followed Prince of Lincheng Xiao Dalian, who made him marshal and gave him the army.

sentences.zh: 異性殘暴，無遠略，督責大連軍主及以左右私樹威福，眾並患之。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was cruel and violent, without far-reaching plans; he pressed Dalian's army commanders and used his intimates to build personal power—all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was cruel and shortsighted; he squeezed Dalian's commanders and used favorites to build private power, and all hated him.

sentences.zh: 會景將軍宋子仙濟浙江，異奔還鄉里，尋以其眾降于子仙。

translations.literal: When Jing's general Song Zixian crossed the Zhe River Yi fled home and soon surrendered his host to Zixian.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing's general Song Zixian crossed the Zhe, Yi fled home and soon surrendered his troops to him.

sentences.zh: 是時大連亦趣東陽之信安嶺，欲之鄱陽，異乃為子仙鄉導，令執大連。

translations.literal: Dalian also was hurrying to Dongyang's Xin'an Ridge intending to go to Poyang; Yi then guided Zixian and had him seize Dalian.
translations.idiomatic: Dalian was also hurrying toward Xin'an Ridge in Dongyang, bound for Poyang. Yi guided Zixian and had him seize Dalian.

sentences.zh: 侯景署異為東陽太守，收其妻子為質。

translations.literal: Hou Jing appointed Yi Dongyang prefect and took his wife and children as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing made Yi Dongyang prefect and held his wife and children hostage.

sentences.zh: 景行臺劉神茂建義拒景，異外同神茂，而密契於景。

translations.literal: Jing's field secretariat Liu Shenmao raised righteousness against Jing; Yi outwardly joined Shenmao but secretly was pledged to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's field secretariat chief Liu Shenmao turned against him. Yi pretended to join Shenmao but secretly kept faith with Jing.

sentences.zh: 及神茂敗績，為景所誅，異獨獲免。

translations.literal: When Shenmao was defeated Jing executed him; Yi alone escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenmao was beaten Jing killed him; Yi alone was spared.

sentences.zh: 侯景平後，王僧辯使異慰勞東陽，仍糾合鄉閭，保據巖阻，其徒甚盛，州郡憚焉。

translations.literal: After Hou Jing was pacified Wang Sengbian sent Yi to comfort Dongyang; he still mustered home districts and held rugged passes; his band was very strong and prefectures and commanderies feared him.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing was crushed Wang Sengbian sent Yi to reassure Dongyang, but Yi still rallied the countryside and held the passes. His following was huge, and the region feared him.

sentences.zh: 元帝以為信安令。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan made him magistrate of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan made him magistrate of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 荊州陷，王僧辯以異為東陽太守。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou fell Wang Sengbian made him Dongyang prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou fell Wang Sengbian made him Dongyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 世祖平定會稽，異雖轉輸糧饋，而擁擅一郡，威福在己。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen pacified Kuaiji Yi though forwarded grain rations still monopolized a whole commandery—authority and favor were his alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took Kuaiji, Yi sent grain but still kept the whole commandery in his grip, with power and favor his alone.

sentences.zh: 紹泰二年，以應接之功，除持節、通直散騎常侍、信武將軍、縉州刺史，領東陽太守，封永興縣侯，[7]邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Shaotai year 2, for supporting-joining merit, appointed bearer of credentials, direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, trust-military general, inspector of Jingzhou, concurrently Dongyang prefect, enfeoffed marquis of Yongxing county, [7] fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 2, for aiding the court, he was made bearer of credentials, direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry, trust-military general, inspector of Jingzhou with concurrent Dongyang prefect, and marquis of Yongxing county [7] with a fief of five hundred households. On [7]: the Southern History reads Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 其年遷散騎常侍、信威將軍，增邑三百戶，餘並如故。

translations.literal: That year he was promoted to scattered-cavalry regular attendant and trust-prestige general; the fief increased by three hundred households; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year he rose to scattered-cavalry regular attendant and trust-prestige general, with three hundred more households in the fief; other posts were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又以世祖長女豐安公主配異第三子貞臣。

translations.literal: Also Emperor Wen's eldest daughter Princess Feng'an was matched to Yi's third son Zhenchen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen also gave his eldest daughter, Princess Feng'an, to Yi's third son Zhenchen.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，徵異為使持節、散騎常侍、都督南徐州諸軍事、平北將軍、南徐州刺史，異遷延不就。

translations.literal: Yongding year 2 he was summoned as bearer of credentials, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou military affairs, pacify-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou; Yi delayed and would not come.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2 he was summoned as bearer of credentials, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou, pacify-north general, and inspector of South Xuzhou. Yi stalled and never came.

sentences.zh: 昔四罪難弘，大媯之所無赦，九黎亂德，少昊之所必誅。

translations.literal: Of old the four crimes were hard to pardon—Great Gun had none the Great Regulator spared; the Nine Li corrupted virtue—Shaohao surely executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Of old the four crimes were hard to spare: Great Gun found no pardon from the Great Regulator; the Nine Li corrupted virtue, and Shaohao surely put them to death.

sentences.zh: 自古皇王，不貪征伐，苟為時蠹，事非獲已。

translations.literal: Since antiquity emperors and kings have not coveted campaigns; when a man is the age's pest, affairs leave no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity kings have not loved war; when a man is the age's pest, they act because they must.

sentences.zh: 逆賊留異，數應亡滅，繕甲完聚，由來積年。

translations.literal: The rebel Yi should many times have perished; he has mustered armor and gathered forces for years.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Yi should long since have perished; for years he has kept armor bright and hosts gathered.

sentences.zh: 進謝群龍，自躍於千里，退懷首鼠，恆持於百心。

translations.literal: Advancing he declined the assembled dragons yet leaped a thousand li; retreating he harbored the rat's two minds and always held a hundred hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Coming forward he refused the court's grace yet sprang a thousand li; drawing back he played the wavering rat and kept a hundred schemes.

sentences.zh: 中歲密契番禺，既弘天網，賜以名爵，敦以國姻，儻望懷音，猶能革面。

translations.literal: In mid-years he secretly pledged Panyu; the heavenly net was already spread wide and he was granted titles and names, bound by a state marriage—if only he would heed the call he might still change his face.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-life he secretly tied himself to Panyu. The court spread the heavenly net, gave him rank and a princess marriage—had he listened, he might still have turned his face.

sentences.zh: 王琳竊據中流，翻相應接，別引南川之嶺路，專為東道之主人，結附凶渠，唯欣禍亂。

translations.literal: Wang Lin seized the middle reaches and in turn answered him; he opened another southern route over the ranges and made himself sole host of the eastern road, clinging to vicious chiefs and rejoicing only in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin held the middle Yangtze and answered him in turn. He opened another mountain route south and made himself master of the eastern road, clinging to villains and welcoming chaos.

sentences.zh: 既祅氛盪定，氣沮心孤，類傷鳥之驚弦，等窮獸之謀觸。

translations.literal: Once the evil vapors were swept away his spirit flagged and his heart stood alone—like a wounded bird at the bowstring, like a cornered beast planning a desperate strike.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were crushed his spirit sank and he stood alone—like a bird still flinching at the bow, like a beast at bay planning one last rush.

sentences.zh: 雖復遣家入質，子陽之態轉遒；

translations.literal: Though again he sent his family as hostages, Ziyang's manner grew only fiercer;
translations.idiomatic: Though he again sent his family as hostages, his manner grew only fiercer, like Ziyang;

sentences.zh: 侍子還朝，隗囂之心方熾。

translations.literal: when the hostage son returned to court Wei Xiao's heart burned only hotter.
translations.idiomatic: and when the hostage son returned to court his heart burned hotter still, like Wei Xiao.

sentences.zh: 朕志相成養，不計疵慝，披襟解帶，敦喻殷勤。

translations.literal: We are minded to nurture mutual completion, not counting faults and flaws, opening breast and loosening belt, earnestly instructing.
translations.idiomatic: We meant to nurture him to completion, overlooking every fault, opening our breast and speaking with all earnestness.

sentences.zh: 蜂目彌彰，梟聲無改，遂置軍江口，嚴戍下淮，顯然反叛，非可容匿。

translations.literal: His owl eyes shone clearer; his owl cry never changed; he then set troops at the river mouth and strict guards below Huai—open rebellion that could not be hidden.
translations.idiomatic: His owl eyes shone the brighter; his owl cry never changed. He set troops at the river mouth and strict guards below the Huai—open rebellion that could not be concealed.

sentences.zh: 且縉邦膏腴，稽南殷曠，永割王賦，長壅國民，竹箭良材，絕望京輦，萑蒲小盜，共肆貪殘，念彼餘甿，兼其慨息。

translations.literal: Moreover Jing prefecture is rich soil and south of Kuaiji broad and populous; he forever cut off royal tax and long choked the people; fine bamboo and good timber never reached the capital carriage; petty reeds-and-rushes bandits together indulged greedy cruelty—thinking of those remaining folk doubles our sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was rich land and south Kuaiji teemed with people, yet he forever withheld the royal tax and choked the folk. Fine bamboo never reached the capital; petty bandits plundered with him. To think of those who remained is to sigh twice.

sentences.zh: 西戎屈膝，自款重關，秦國依風，並輸侵地，三邊已乂，四表咸寧，唯此微妖，所宜清殄。

translations.literal: Western Rong bent the knee and came in at the heavy passes; Qin submitted to the wind and together yielded invaded lands; the three marches are already at peace and the four quarters all secure—only this petty demon should be swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Western tribes knelt at the passes; Qin came over and returned seized lands; the three marches are quiet and the four quarters secure—only this petty demon should be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 可遣使持節、都督南徐州諸軍事、征北將軍、司空、南徐州刺史桂陽郡開國公安都指往擒戮，罪止異身，餘無所問。

translations.literal: Let bearer of credentials, commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou military affairs, campaign-north general, minister of works, inspector of South Xuzhou, and founding duke of Guiyang commandery Andu go to seize and execute; guilt rests on Yi alone; the rest are not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Let bearer of credentials, commander-in-chief of South Xuzhou, campaign-north general, minister of works, inspector of South Xuzhou, and founding duke of Guiyang Andu go to seize and kill him. Guilt rests on Yi alone; no one else will be punished.

sentences.zh: 異本謂官軍自錢塘江而上，安都乃由會稽、諸暨步道襲之。

translations.literal: Yi had expected the government army to come up the Qiantang River; Andu instead marched overland through Kuaiji and Zhuji to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi expected the imperial army up the Qiantang. Andu marched overland through Kuaiji and Zhuji instead.

sentences.zh: 異聞兵至，大恐，棄郡奔于桃支嶺，於嶺口立柵自固。

translations.literal: When Yi heard the army had come he was greatly afraid, abandoned the commandery, and fled to Taozhi Ridge; at the pass mouth he set palisades to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the army had come, Yi was terrified, left the commandery, and fled to Taozhi Ridge, where he walled the pass.

sentences.zh: 明年春，安都大破其柵，異與第二子忠臣奔于陳寶應，於是虜其餘黨男女數千人。

translations.literal: Next spring Andu greatly broke his palisades; Yi and his second son Chuxin fled to Chen Baoying; his remaining partisans, men and women numbering several thousand, were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring Andu smashed the palisades. Yi and his second son Chuxin fled to Chen Baoying. Several thousand followers, men and women, were taken.

sentences.zh: 天嘉五年，陳寶應平，并擒異送都，斬于建康市，子姪及同黨無少長皆伏誅，唯第三子貞臣以尚主獲免。

translations.literal: Tianjia year 5, when Chen Baoying was pacified Yi was also seized and sent to the capital and beheaded in Jiankang market; sons, nephews, and fellow conspirators of every age were executed; only the third son Zhenchen was spared for having married the princess.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 5, when Chen Baoying fell, Yi was seized, sent to the capital, and beheaded in the Jiankang market. Sons, nephews, and allies of every age were killed; only the third son Zhenchen was spared because he had married the princess.

sentences.zh: 陳寶應，晉安候官人也。

translations.literal: Chen Baoying was a man of Houguan in Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baoying came from Houguan in Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 世為閩中四姓。

translations.literal: His family for generations were one of the four great surnames of Min.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his clan was one of Min's four great surnames.

sentences.zh: 父羽，有材幹，為郡雄豪。

translations.literal: His father Yu had talent and ability and was a commandery strongman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was capable and a commandery magnate.

sentences.zh: 寶應性反覆，多變詐。

translations.literal: Baoying's nature was changeable and full of shifting deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying was fickle and steeped in deceit.

sentences.zh: 梁代晉安數反，累殺郡將，羽初並扇惑合成其事，後復為官軍鄉導破之，由是一郡兵權皆自己出。

translations.literal: In Liang times Jin'an rebelled many times and repeatedly killed commandery chiefs; at first Yu together incited and completed the affair, then again served as guide for government troops to break them—thereafter all military power of the commandery issued from himself.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang Jin'an rose repeatedly and killed its prefects. Yu first stirred the rebels, then guided government troops to crush them, and from then on held the commandery's military power.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，晉安太守、賓化侯蕭雲以郡讓羽，羽年老，但治郡事，令寶應典兵。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled Jin'an prefect Marquis of Binhua Xiao Yun yielded the commandery to Yu; Yu was old and only handled commandery affairs, putting Baoying in charge of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Jin'an prefect Marquis of Binhua Xiao Yun yielded the commandery to Yu. Yu was old and ran civil affairs while Baoying commanded the troops.

sentences.zh: 是時東境饑饉，會稽尤甚，死者十七八，平民男女，並皆自賣，而晉安獨豐沃。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern lands were in famine; Kuaiji was worst; seven or eight in ten died; common men and women all sold themselves, yet Jin'an alone was rich and fertile.
translations.idiomatic: The east was starving; Kuaiji was worst, with seven or eight in ten dead. Families sold themselves, yet Jin'an alone stayed rich.

sentences.zh: 寶應自海道寇臨安、永嘉及會稽、餘姚、諸暨，[8]又載米粟與之貿易，多致玉帛子女，其有能致舟乘者，亦並奔歸之，由是大致貲產，士眾彊盛。

translations.literal: Baoying by sea raided Lin'an, Yongjia, Kuaiji, Yuyao, and Zhuji, [8] and also carried rice and grain to trade with them, gaining much silks, jades, and women; those who could bring boats also all fled to join him—thereby he amassed great wealth and his soldiers and masses were strong.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying raided by sea at Linhai [8], Yongjia, Kuaiji, Yuyao, and Zhuji, and traded rice and grain for silks, jades, and women. On [8]: Lin'an in the base text should be Linhai. Whoever could sail a boat joined him, and he grew very rich and strong.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，元帝因以羽為晉安太守。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified Emperor Yuan therefore made Yu Jin'an prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was crushed Emperor Yuan made Yu Jin'an prefect.

sentences.zh: 寶應娶留異女為妻，侯安都之討異也，寶應遣兵助之，又資周迪兵糧，出寇臨川。

translations.literal: Baoying married Liu Yi's daughter; when Hou Andu campaigned against Yi, Baoying sent troops to help and also supplied Zhou Di with grain and arms, raiding out at Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying married Liu Yi's daughter. When Hou Andu attacked Yi, Baoying sent troops to help and supplied Zhou Di with grain, then raided Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 及都督章昭達於東興、南城破迪，世祖因命昭達都督眾軍，由建安南道渡嶺，又命益州刺史領信義太守余孝頃都督會稽、東陽、臨海、永嘉諸軍自東道會之，以討寶應，并詔宗正絕其屬籍。

translations.literal: When area commander Zhang Zhaoda defeated Di at Dongxing and Nancheng, Emperor Wen then ordered Zhaoda to command all armies south over the ranges by the Jian'an road, and also ordered inspector of Yizhou and concurrent Xinyi prefect Yu Xiaoding to command armies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, and Yongjia from the east to join, to campaign against Baoying, and also ordered the director of imperial clan affairs to strike him from the genealogical register.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhaoda beat Di at Dongxing and Nancheng, Emperor Wen put Zhaoda over all forces crossing south by the Jian'an road and ordered Yizhou inspector Yu Xiaoding, also Xinyi prefect, to strike from the east through Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, and Yongjia. The clan director was told to erase Baoying from the register.

sentences.zh: 於是尚書下符曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon the Masters of Writing issued a dispatch saying:
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing then issued a dispatch:

sentences.zh: 告晉安士庶：昔隴西旅拒，漢不稽誅，遼東叛換，魏申宏略。

translations.literal: To the gentry and commoners of Jin'an: of old Longxi's brigands resisted and Han did not delay punishment; Liaodong rebelled and changed allegiance and Wei set forth a great plan.
translations.idiomatic: To the people of Jin'an: Longxi once resisted and Han did not delay punishment; Liaodong rebelled and Wei laid down a great plan.

sentences.zh: 若夫無諸漢之策勳，有扈夏之同姓，至於納吳濞之子，致橫海之師，違姒啟之命，有甘誓之討。

translations.literal: As for Wu Ru's merit under Han and Youhu's kinship under Xia—down to taking Wu Pi's son and bringing the armies of the Four Seas, defying Si Qi's command and incurring the punitive oath of Gan—
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ru served Han; Youhu shared Xia's kinship; one took Wu Pi's son and raised the armies of the Four Seas; another defied Si Qi and met the oath of Gan—

sentences.zh: 況迺族不繫於宗盟，名無紀於庸器，而顯成三叛，舋深四罪者乎？

translations.literal: how much more when clan is not tied to the ancestral alliance and name is not recorded among ordinary vessels, yet plainly completing three rebellions and guilt reaching the four crimes?
translations.idiomatic: how much more when a clan is not bound to the royal house, its name not listed among the worthy, yet plainly commits three rebellions and guilt as deep as the four crimes?

sentences.zh: 案閩寇陳寶應父子，卉服支孽，本迷愛敬。

translations.literal: We find the Min bandit Chen Baoying father and son—barbarian dress, branch offshoots—originally lost to love and respect.
translations.idiomatic: We find the Min bandits Chen Baoying and his father—savage dress, a side branch—who from the first forgot love and respect.

sentences.zh: 梁季喪亂，閩隅阻絕，父既豪俠，扇動蠻陬，椎髻箕坐，自為渠帥，無聞訓義，所資姦諂，爰肆蜂豺，俄而解印。

translations.literal: Liang's age fell into chaos; the Min corner was cut off; the father was bold and stirred the barbarian hills; with topknots and squatting like chiefs they heard no instruction in righteousness and relied on flattery and deceit, then suddenly let fall the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Liang fell into chaos and Min was cut off. The father was bold and stirred the hill tribes; with topknots they sat as chiefs, knowing no rites, trusting only flattery, then cast off the seal.

sentences.zh: 炎行方謝，網漏吞舟，日月居諸，棄之度外。

translations.literal: The Han line was ending; the net leaked even great fish; days and months rolled on and they were cast beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Han line was ending; the net let great fish through; time passed and they were left outside the law.

sentences.zh: 自東南王氣，寔表聖基，斗牛聚星，允符王跡，梯山航海，雖若款誠，擅割瑰珍，竟微職貢。

translations.literal: Since the southeast's royal qi truly marked the holy foundation and the Dipper and Ox gathered stars truly matched the royal trace, though scaling mountains and crossing seas seemed like sincere submission, they privately cut off gems and jewels and in the end offered scant tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Southeastern royal qi marked the new throne; Dipper and Ox stars matched the royal trace. Though they seemed to come over mountains and seas in submission, they kept gems for themselves and barely paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遵養含弘，寵靈隆赫，起家臨郡，兼晝繡之榮，裂地置州，假藩麾之盛。

translations.literal: The court followed nurture and held forbearance; favor and glory were lofty and bright; he rose from home to govern a commandery with the glory of daytime brocade; land was split to set a province and the splendor of a frontier banner was lent.
translations.idiomatic: The court nurtured and bore with them, heaping favor: from home to commandery with brocade glory by day; land split into a province and a commander's banner lent.

sentences.zh: 即封戶牖，仍邑櫟陽，乘華轂者十人，保弊廬而萬石。

translations.literal: At once households were enfeoffed and still enfeoffed at Liyang; ten men rode ornamented carriages while ten thousand stone salaries guarded humble huts.
translations.idiomatic: Households were enfeoffed at once, with Liyang still in the fief; ten men rode fine carriages while ten-thousand-bushel pay guarded poor roofs.

sentences.zh: 又以盛漢君臨，推恩婁敬，隆周朝會，迺長滕侯，由是紫泥青紙，遠賁恩澤，鄉亭龜組，頒及嬰孩。

translations.literal: Again, as flourishing Han ruled all, favor was pushed as with Lou Jing; as grand Zhou held court Teng was made long marquis—thereby purple mud and blue paper bore favor from afar and district and village tortoise seals reached even infants.
translations.idiomatic: As Han ruled all, favor spread like Lou Jing's; as Zhou held court Teng was made long marquis—purple edicts and blue paper came from afar, tortoise seals from district and village even to infants.

sentences.zh: 自谷遷喬，孰復為擬，而苞藏鴆毒，敢行狼戾。

translations.literal: From valley to tall tree, what could compare—yet he harbored poison and dared wolfish outrage.
translations.idiomatic: From low to high, what could match it—yet he hid poison and dared wolfish outrage.

sentences.zh: 連結留異，表裏周迪，盟歃婚姻，自為脣齒，屈彊山谷，推移歲時。

translations.literal: He linked with Liu Yi inside and out with Zhou Di; oaths and marriage made them lip and teeth; strong in the mountain valleys they shifted with the years.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Liu Yi and Zhou Di, oath and marriage making them lip and teeth, strong in the hills year after year.

sentences.zh: 及我彀騎防山，定秦望之西部，戈船下瀨，克匯澤之南川，遂敢舉斧，並助凶孽，莫不應弦摧衄，盡殪醜徒。

translations.literal: When our armed riders guarded the mountains and fixed the western part of Qinwang's outlook, and war-boats went down the rapids and took the southern streams of Huize, they then dared raise the axe and together aid the vicious brood—none failed to break at the bowstring and all the ugly crew were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: When our cavalry held the mountains and took Qinwang's western flank, and war-boats swept Huize's southern streams, they still raised the axe to aid the rebels—every one broke at the string and the whole wicked band was killed.

sentences.zh: 每以罪在酋渠，憫茲驅逼，所收俘馘，並勒矜放。

translations.literal: Each time guilt lay with the chiefs we pitied those driven on; captives taken were all ordered released in mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Each time guilt lay with the chiefs we pitied those they drove; captives were ordered released.

sentences.zh: 仍遣中使，爰降詔書，天網恢弘，猶許改思。

translations.literal: We still sent palace envoys and lowered edicts; the heavenly net was vast and still allowed change of mind.
translations.idiomatic: We still sent palace envoys with edicts; the heavenly net was wide and still allowed repentance.

sentences.zh: 異既走險，迪又逃刑，誑侮王人，為之川藪，遂使袁熙請席，遠歎頭行，馬援觀蛙，猶安井底。

translations.literal: Yi had already fled to peril and Di had escaped punishment; they deceived and insulted the king's men and made themselves a mountain lair—so Yuan Xi asked for a mat and sighed far off at Touxing's march, and Ma Yuan watched frogs yet was content in the well bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had fled to the hills and Di had escaped justice. They mocked the king's officers and made a mountain lair—like Yuan Xi asking for a mat and sighing at Touxing far away, like Ma Yuan watching frogs content in a well.

sentences.zh: 至如遏絕九賦，剽掠四民，闔境資財，盡室封奪，凡厥倉頭，皆略黔首。

translations.literal: As for cutting off the nine levies, plundering the four peoples, seizing all wealth within the borders and stripping every household, every bondservant was looted from the black-haired folk.
translations.idiomatic: They cut off the nine taxes, plundered the four orders, seized all wealth in the region and stripped every house, and every bondservant was taken from the people.

sentences.zh: 蝥賊相扇，協契連蹤，乃復踰超瀛溟，寇擾浹口，侵軼嶺嶠，掩襲述城，縛掠吏民，焚燒官寺，此而可縱，孰不可容？

translations.literal: Bandits fanned one another in league and track; they again crossed beyond the ocean, raided Jia mouth, pressed the range passes, and stormed Shucheng, binding officials and people and burning government temples—if this may be indulged, what may not be borne?
translations.idiomatic: Bandits stirred one another and again crossed the sea, raided Jia mouth, struck the passes, stormed Shucheng, bound officials and people, and burned government temples—if this is allowed, what is not?

sentences.zh: 今遣沙州刺史俞文冏，明威將軍程文季，假節、宣猛將軍、成州刺史甘他，假節、雲旗將軍譚瑱，假節、宣猛將軍、前監臨海郡陳思慶，前軍將軍徐智遠，明毅將軍宜黃縣開國侯慧紀，開遠將軍、新除晉安太守趙彖，持節、通直散騎常侍、壯武將軍、定州刺史康樂縣開國侯林馮，假節、信威將軍、都督東討諸軍事、益州刺史余孝頃，率羽林二萬，蒙衝蓋海，乘跨滄波，掃蕩巢窟。

translations.literal: Now sent are Shazhou inspector Yu Wenjiong, bright-prestige general Cheng Wenji, acting bearer of credentials and fierce-assault general and Chengzou inspector Gan Ta, acting bearer of credentials and cloud-banner general Tan Zhen, acting bearer of credentials and fierce-assault general and former overseer of Linhai commandery Chen Sijing, vanguard general Xu Zhiyuan, bright-resolve general and founding marquis of Yihuang Huaiji, open-distance general and newly appointed Jin'an prefect Zhao Can, bearer of credentials and direct regular attendant of scattered cavalry and stalwart-military general and Dingzhou inspector and founding marquis of Kangle Lin Feng, acting bearer of credentials and trust-prestige general and commander-in-chief of eastern campaign military affairs and Yizhou inspector Yu Xiaoding—leading twenty thousand feathered guards, war-junks covering the sea, riding the blue waves to sweep the nest and den.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shazhou inspector Yu Wenjiong, bright-prestige general Cheng Wenji, acting credential-bearer and fierce-assault general Gan Ta of Chengzou, acting credential-bearer and cloud-banner general Tan Zhen, acting credential-bearer and fierce-assault general Chen Sijing, former overseer of Linhai, vanguard general Xu Zhiyuan, bright-resolve general and founding marquis of Yihuang Huaiji, open-distance general and new Jin'an prefect Zhao Can, credential-bearer and direct regular attendant Lin Feng of Dingzhou, and acting credential-bearer Yu Xiaoding of Yizhou, commander of the eastern campaign, lead twenty thousand guards. War-junks cover the sea to sweep the nest clean.

sentences.zh: 此皆明恥教戰，濡須鞠旅，[9]累從楊僕，亟走孫恩，斬蛟中流，命馮夷而鳴鼓，黿鼉為駕，轥方壺而建旗。

translations.literal: These all understand shame and teach war; at Ruxu they array troops, [9] repeatedly followed Yang Pu, often chased Sun En, cut the flood-dragon midstream and ordered Feng Yi to beat drums, took turtle and alligator for chariot and rolled over Fanghu to raise banners.
translations.idiomatic: They know shame and teach war; at Ruxu they drill [9], followed Yang Pu again and again, chased Sun En repeatedly, cut the flood-dragon midstream and ordered Feng Yi to drum, drove turtle and alligator as chariot and raised banners over Fanghu. On [9]: the Ruxu camp reference is not corrupt.

sentences.zh: 義安太守張紹賓，忠誠款到，累使求軍，南康內史裴忌，新除輕車將軍劉峰，東衡州刺史錢道戢，並即遣人仗，與紹賓同行。

translations.literal: Yi'an prefect Zhang Shaobin, loyal and sincere in arrival, repeatedly sent asking for troops; Nankang interior administrator Pei Ji, newly appointed light-chariot general Liu Feng, and Donghengzhou inspector Qian Daozhi all at once sent men and arms to march with Shaobin.
translations.idiomatic: Yi'an prefect Zhang Shaobin came in loyalty and begged for troops again and again. Nankang interior administrator Pei Ji, new light-chariot general Liu Feng, and Donghengzhou inspector Qian Daozhi all sent men and arms to march with him.

sentences.zh: 故司空歐陽公，昔有表奏，請宣薄伐，遙途意合，若伏波之論兵，長逝遺誠，同子顏之勿赦。

translations.literal: The late minister of works Lord Ouyang in old days had a memorial asking to proclaim a limited campaign; across the distance his intent matched, like Fubo on warfare; long gone he left a testament, the same as Ziyan's "do not spare."
translations.idiomatic: The late minister of works Lord Ouyang once memorialized for a limited campaign; his intent matched ours across the distance, like Fubo's talk of war. Dead, he left a charge like Ziyan's "do not spare."

sentences.zh: 征南薨謝，上策無忘，周南餘恨，嗣子弗忝。

translations.literal: The campaign-south lord has died; the upper plan is not forgotten; Zhounan's remaining regret—the heir son will not fail it.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign-south lord is gone, but the upper plan is not forgotten. Zhounan's remaining regret—the heir will not fail it.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史歐陽紇，克符家聲，聿遵廣略，舟師步卒，二萬分趨，水扼長鯨，陸掣封狶，董率衡、廣之師，會我六軍。

translations.literal: Guangzhou inspector Ouyang He fulfills the family name and follows the broad plan; river army and foot soldiers twenty thousand divide and hurry; on water he checks the long whale, on land he reins the great boar, leading Heng and Guang troops to join our six armies.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou inspector Ouyang He keeps the family name and follows the broad plan. Twenty thousand men by river and land hurry forward; on water he blocks the long whale, on land he reins the great boar, leading Heng and Guang to join our six armies.

sentences.zh: 潼州刺史李䐗，[10]明州刺史戴晃，新州刺史區白獸，[11]壯武將軍脩行師，陳留太守張遂，前安成內史闕慎，前廬陵太守陸子隆，前豫寧太守任蠻奴，[12]巴山太守黃法慈，戎昭將軍、湘東公世子徐敬成，吳州刺史魯廣達，前吳州刺史遂興縣開國侯詳，使持節、都督征討諸軍事、散騎常侍、護軍將軍昭達，率緹騎五千，組甲二萬，直渡邵武，仍頓晉安。

translations.literal: Tongzhou inspector Li La, [10] Mingzhou inspector Dai Huang, Xinzhou inspector Qu Baishou, [11] stalwart-military general Xiu Xingshi, Chenliu prefect Zhang Sui, former Angu interior administrator Que Shen, former Luling prefect Lu Zilong, former Yuning prefect Ren Mannu, [12] Bashan prefect Huang Fahui, martial-display general and heir of the Duke of Xiangdong Xu Jingcheng, Wu prefect Lu Guangda, former Wu prefect and founding marquis of Suixing Xiang, bearer of credentials and commander-in-chief of campaign military affairs and scattered-cavalry regular attendant and protector general Zhaoda—leading five thousand brocade cavalry and twenty thousand mailed men, crossing straight at Shaowu and then encamping at Jin'an.
